question.text: A portfolio manager constructs an ESG portfolio by excluding tobacco, gambling, and weapons manufacturers while including all other investable universe. This screening approach is called:

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Negative screening = exclusion of offending sectors. Positive screening rates/ranks on ESG scores and picks top quantile. Best-in-class picks top-ranked within each sector. **The Trap:** All three are ESG approaches — the distinction is whether you're excluding, selecting top ESG, or selecting top-per-sector. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B AIF Distributors discuss ESG as a thematic asset class; X-A covers it for adviser product selection. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Best-in-class preserves sector diversification (you still own a tobacco if it's the best-governed) — suits mandates that can't tolerate sector drift.
